result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks on both sides and a stop-controlled intersection with a marked crosswalk. However, the environment lacks physical buffers between pedestrians and traffic, and parked vehicles near the intersection may obstruct sightlines for crossing.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parking
hazards.description: Parallel parked cars extend close to the intersection, potentially blocking the view between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both sides of the street approaching the intersection.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the curb with no planting strip or furniture zone to separate pedestrians from moving vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the foreground street.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility (daylighting).

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or a raised intersection to reduce vehicle speeds in this residential/mixed-use context.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, well-maintained concrete sidewalk adjacent to a multi-story brick building and a residential house. There is no physical buffer between the walkway and the roadway, and on-street parallel parking is present, which may obstruct sightlines.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian-vehicle buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the travel and parking lane with no physical separation like a planting strip or bollards.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line throughout the foreground.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars can obscure pedestrians, especially children, from the view of oncoming drivers if they attempt to cross mid-block.
hazards.location_in_image: Red car parked on the right side of the frame.

interventions.title: Install Street Trees or Planters
interventions.description: Adding a furniture zone with trees or planters would provide a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and moving traffic.

interventions.title: Add Street Lighting
interventions.description: Install pedestrian-scale street lighting to improve visibility and safety during nighttime hours.

result.summary: A narrow residential street with row houses and continuous sidewalks on both sides. The environment is characterized by high-density on-street parking and a lack of marked pedestrian crossings or traffic calming measures.

hazards.name: Visibility obstruction from parked cars
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the narrow street creates sightline issues between drivers and pedestrians, particularly children, who might step out from between cars.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the visible block

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the far intersection to improve visibility and shorten the crossing distance.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Add speed humps to physically enforce low vehicle speeds in this residential area.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to improve sightlines.
